column1: # MINING TERMS — Burmese (my). Read by `mine.ts --terms`, for the LEXICAL cells only.
# WHY THIS FILE IS COMMITTED. `my.jsonc` is the one artifact in the tree mined from a full Wikipedia dump
# rather than FLEURS, and it is the best-covered one — 454,821 segments, every cell of the inventory it was
# measured against. Two of those cells are LEXICAL (`calendar`, `ordinal-native`): they are found by matching
# the language's own WORDS, not by a shape, so they cannot be filled without a term list. The list used
# originally was a scratch file and was never committed, which meant the tree's richest artifact could not be
# regenerated from the repository at all — the #586 re-mine hit exactly that wall (calendar alone holds 81,301
# occurrences and would simply have vanished).
# `cell<TAB>term` scopes a term to one cell; a bare line applies to every lexical cell. The two cells need
# different words, which is why the scoping exists.
# PROVENANCE. Every month name below except ဇွန် is corroborated in the repo's own Burmese data
# (`src/languages/burmese/dictionary.tsv`, `seg-words.txt`); ဇွန် is absent from those files, and was checked
# through the phonemizer instead — it reads as `zʊ˨ɴ` from the g2p rules, so its absence is a dictionary gap
# and not a missing reading. The ordinals are the Pali-derived series, all ten corroborated in the same files.
# Checked mechanically: of the 22 terms here, ဇွန် is the only one absent from the repo's Burmese data.
# These are SEARCH terms, not pronunciation data: a wrong one costs recall in one cell, never a wrong reading.
# ── calendar: the Gregorian month names as Burmese Wikipedia writes them ──
